ford-71416.text:
At Ford Motor Company, we believe freedom of movement drives human progress. We also believe in providing you with the freedom to define and realize your dreams. With our incredible plans for the future of mobility, we have a wide variety of opportunities for you to accelerate your career potential as you help us define tomorrow’s transportation.
Creating the future of smart mobility requires the highly intelligent use of data, metrics, and analytics. That’s where you can make an impact as part of our Global Data Insight & Analytics (GDIA) team. We are the trusted advisers that enable Ford to clearly see business conditions, customer needs, and the competitive landscape. With our support, key decision-makers can act in meaningful, positive ways. Join us and use your data expertise and analytical skills to drive evidence-based, timely decision-making.
Position Overview
Industrial Systems Analytics (ISA) is a product group that develops cutting-edge, on-premises and cloud analytic solutions. We are modernizing our portfolio by embedding Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and autonomous agentic workflows to revolutionize how Ford manages industrial data.
This Software Engineer position is ideal for a technically oriented, forward-thinking individual who has experience designing, building, and deploying cloud applications, and who is eager to pioneer the use of Agentic AI and LLMs to solve complex industrial analytics challenges.
What You’ll Be Able To Do
As a Full-Stack Software Engineer on our Balanced Product Team, you will collaborate closely with Product Managers, Product Designers, and fellow engineers to deliver next-generation analytical solutions. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of these solutions—from design and development to deployment, maintenance, and AI-driven optimization.
AI & Agentic Solution Development: Architect, build, and deploy LLM-powered applications, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, and multi-agent systems to automate complex data analysis, anomaly detection, and decision-support workflows.
AI-Assisted Software Engineering: Champion the use of generative AI tools and agentic coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, custom LLM agents) to streamline the software development lifecycle, automate testing, and accelerate CI/CD pipelines.
Product & Requirements Management: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate business goals into technical requirements, user stories, and test suites within an Agile framework.
Technical Design & Architecture: Author comprehensive technical design documents, system architecture diagrams, and API specifications to ensure scalable, secure, and maintainable solutions.
Modern Operations & DevOps: Build robust CI/CD deployment pipelines, integrate automated security/quality scanning, and implement modern Identity & Access Management (IAM) and automated credential rotation.
Reliability & Continuous Improvement: Participate in proactive problem management, root cause analysis (RCA), and incident resolution to ensure high availability of critical analytical systems.
Minimum Requirements We Seek
Requires a bachelor’s or foreign equivalent degree in computer science, information technology or a technology related field.
4+ years of professional experience in Software Engineering.
3+ years of experience with modern frontend frameworks (Angular, React, or Vue).
3+ years of experience with backend frameworks (FastAPI, Flask, Django, or Spring Boot).
2+ years of experience with Python (highly preferred for AI/Data) and/or Java.
Exposure to or hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex AI) or open-source models into software applications.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
AI & Agentic Frameworks: Proven experience working with LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex) and multi-agent development platforms (e.g., CrewAI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel).
Vector Databases & Data Pipelines: Familiarity with vector databases (e.g., PGVector, Chroma, Pinecone, Milvus) and embedding techniques for semantic search and RAG.
Software Craftsmanship: Deep understanding of software engineering disciplines inclu,ding eXtreme Programming (XP), Clean Code principles, Test-Driven Development (TDD), and Pair/Mob programming.
Cloud & DevOps: Experience developing and deploying to cloud platforms (GCP, Azure, or AWS) using modern CI/CD tools (Tekton, Terraform, Jenkins, Cloud Build).
Agile Mindset: Experience working with Agile tools (Jira, Rally) in a fast-paced, collaborative, continuous-delivery environment.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a passion for leveraging cutting-edge technology to amaze and delight our business partners and customers.
You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!
As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:

In this position...
We are seeking a Test Automation Developer to build and maintain Python-based automated testing solutions for embedded automotive connectivity systems. This role combines hands-on software testing and development with the practical use of AI and LLM technologies to enhance requirements analysis, test design, automation, troubleshooting, and software quality.
What you'll do...
Utilize LLM and AI tools to accomplish software analysis and development tasks.
Apply AI-assisted techniques to support requirement analysis, test design, test automation, defect identification, troubleshooting, and test result analysis.
Analyze product requirement documents for Connected Vehicle Applications and translate them into test cases that cover normal paths, error cases, boundary conditions, and unexpected events.
Work in an Agile software development environment to deliver high-quality software solutions for cloud-connected in-vehicle modules operating on CAN and Ethernet networks.
Design, implement, debug, test, and maintain Python-based test automation, including automated scripts that accurately implement test cases for Connected Vehicle Applications.
Execute tests, debug issues, perform root cause analysis, and generate high-quality software defect reports.
Establish and maintain test setups and automated test suite execution.
Develop and maintain software tools, features, and test libraries that support automated testing and interface with vehicle ECUs.
Interface with development and test teams to understand feature functionality and testing requirements.

Review specifications and identify precise product requirements.
Develop and execute functional and integration test plans for feature implementation.
Automate test cases using Python and in-house libraries.
Participate in code reviews and mentor junior developers.
Investigate and reproduce in-vehicle networking issues and verify software fixes.
Contribute to team deliverables through involvement in Agile Scrum development sprints.
Share ideas for innovation, AI-enabled opportunities, and process improvements.
You'll have...
Bachelors degree in Computer or Electrical Engineering or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
2+ years of demonstrated general understanding and practical utilization of Large Language Models and Artificial Intelligence.
2+ years of experience applying LLM or AI tools to software analysis, development, testing, test generation, automation, or test result triage.
2+ years of software test experience and/or tools development on embedded OS platforms such as Linux, QNX, or Android.
2+ years of experience with test management tools such as TestRail, version control systems such as Git/GitHub, issue tracking systems such as JIRA, CI environments such as Jenkins, and corporate wikis such as Confluence.
2+ years of experience in Python development and object-oriented design
2+ years of experience mapping requirements and designs to test cases.
2+ years of experience maintaining automated execution of large test suites and triaging test results.
Even better, you may have...
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Strong aptitude for troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal collaboration.
Detail-oriented and adept at detecting and diagnosing software defects.
Ability to work effectively in a multi-site team environment where self-direction and self-motivation are key.
Experience with distributed systems, including embedded-to-cloud interactions.
Experience with continuous integration systems such as Jenkins, testing frameworks, and shell scripting in Unix/Linux.
Experience with data analytics and visualization.
Experience with microcontrollers, electronics assembly, and debugging equipment.
Working knowledge of AUTOSAR, CAN network technologies, automotive diagnostic protocols, Google Protobuf, and database testing.
Experience with Ethernet, TCP, IP address assignment (DHCP), IP routing, DNS, firewalls, and NAT, including tracing and debugging tools such as Wireshark.
Experience with test benches, hardware, and test tools.

The Ford Motor Credit Company team helps put people behind the wheels of great Ford and Lincoln vehicles. By partnering with dealerships, we provide financing, personalized service and professional expertise to thousands of dealers and millions of customers in over one hundred countries around the world.
In this position...
Software Engineer, Enterprise Billing Platform using cutting edge enterprise software, java systems, Application Programming Interface (API) integration, Agile, and Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) workflows.
What you'll do...
About Ford Motor Company & Enterprise Technology: We are the movers of the world and the makers of the future. We get up every day, roll up our sleeves and build a better world -- together. At Ford, we’re all a part of something bigger than ourselves. Are you ready to change the way the world moves?
Enterprise Technology plays a critical part in shaping the future of mobility. If you’re looking for the chance to leverage advanced technology to redefine the transportation landscape, enhance the customer experience and improve people’s lives, this is the opportunity for you. Join us and challenge your IT expertise and analytical skills to help create vehicles that are as smart as you are.
About Ford Credit & Billing Platform: The Ford Motor Credit Company team helps put people behind the wheels of great Ford and Lincoln vehicles. By partnering with dealerships, we provide financing, personalized service and professional expertise to thousands of dealers and millions of customers in over one hundred countries around the world.
The Enterprise Billing Platform creates a unified billing experience by compiling data from multiple sources and generating reoccurring, consistent invoice templates for customers and downstream systems that includes itemized details of payments due and received as well as product/service information as applicable. The Enterprise Billing Platform will support both Ford and Ford Credit globally.
The Opportunity: As a Software Engineer for the Enterprise Billing Platform, you will design, build, and deliver the services that power billing for Ford and Ford Credit. Working primarily in Java, you will partner with Product Managers, Engineering Managers, and fellow engineers to turn roadmap priorities into reliable, scalable, high-quality software. You will help pioneer an AI-enabled software development lifecycle (SDLC), using AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, coding, testing, and delivery while upholding strong engineering standards. We value engineers who are strong in Java and eager to grow across other languages and technologies.
Software Development:
Design, develop, test, and maintain backend services and APIs.
Build integrations with upstream and downstream systems.
Contribute to full stack development.
AI-Enabled SDLC:
Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., code assistants and LLM-based agents) to accelerate design.
Identify bottlenecks in the traditional SDLC and help introduce AI-enabled practices and automation.
Evaluate AI-generated output for correctness, security, and maintainability.
Share learnings and champion responsible, effective AI adoption.
Collaboration & Agile Delivery:
Work closely with stakeholders to refine user stories, estimate work, and deliver features each iteration.
Participate in agile ceremonies.
Collaborate with cross-product teams.
Partner with engineers on upstream and downstream systems.
Quality, Reliability & Operations:
Apply test-driven development and automated testing (unit, integration, and contract).
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and deploy services to cloud environments.
Design solutions that meet security, compliance, and architecture standards.
Define metrics, logging, and dashboards for effective monitoring.
Troubleshoot, debug, and resolve production issues.
Continuous Learning & Growth:
Stay current with emerging technologies, languages, and AI-enabled engineering practices.
Mentor and learn from teammates through pairing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing.
You'll have...
Software Development:
• Design, develop, test, and maintain backend services and APIs for the Enterprise Billing Platform, primarily in Java (e.g., Spring Boot).
• Write clean, well-tested, maintainable code and participate actively in code reviews.
• Build integrations with upstream and downstream systems to compile billing data and generate accurate, consistent invoices.
• Contribute to full stack development and pick up additional languages and frameworks as product needs evolve.
AI-Enabled SDLC:
• Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., code assistants and LLM-based agents) to accelerate design, coding, testing, documentation, and code review.
• Identify bottlenecks in the traditional SDLC and help introduce AI-enabled practices, automation, and tooling to remove them.
• Critically evaluate AI-generated output for correctness, security, and maintainability before it reaches production.
• Share learnings and champion responsible, effective AI adoption across the engineering team.
Collaboration & Agile Delivery:
• Work closely with Product Managers, Engineering Managers, and fellow engineers to refine user stories, estimate work, and deliver features each iteration.
• Participate in agile ceremonies, including stand-ups, iteration planning, backlog refinement, demos, and retrospectives.
• Collaborate with cross-product teams to identify and resolve technical dependencies.
• Partner with engineers on upstream and downstream systems to align on interfaces, enhancements, and system improvements.
Quality, Reliability & Operations:
• Apply test-driven development and automated testing (unit, integration, and contract) to ensure high-quality releases.
• Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and deploy services to cloud environments using containers and modern DevOps practices.
• Design solutions that meet security, compliance, and architecture standards for sensitive financial data.
• Define metrics, logging, and dashboards for effective monitoring and proactive identification of production issues.
• Troubleshoot, debug, and resolve production issues, and take part in root-cause analysis.
Continuous Learning & Growth:
• Stay current with emerging technologies, languages, and AI-enabled engineering practices, and bring new ideas to the team.
• Mentor and learn from teammates through pairing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing.
Even better, you may have...
What You'll Bring:
• 5+ years of professional software development experience.
• Bachelors degree
• Strong proficiency in Java and related frameworks (e.g., Spring/Spring Boot) for building backend services and RESTful APIs.
• Willingness and ability to learn and work in other programming languages and technologies as needed.
• Hands-on experience with, or a strong passion for, AI-enabled development tools and practices across the SDLC.
• Demonstrated understanding and ability to participate in full stack development.
• Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, object-oriented design, and software design patterns.
• Experience with relational and/or NoSQL databases and SQL.
• Experience with automated testing, version control (Git), and CI/CD practices.
• Experience working in an Agile development environment.
• Strong communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to thrive in a rapidly changing environment.
Even Better If You Have:
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
• Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., GCP, Azure, or AWS), containers, and microservices architecture.
• Experience with Lean methodology, eXtreme Programming (including pair programming and TDD), and Domain Driven Design.
• Experience with additional languages such as Python, Kotlin, or TypeScript.
• Experience in the financial technology (FinTech), billing, or payments industry.

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.
Product Development uses design thinking & user experience methods to deliver breakthrough products and services that delight our customers. We bring innovative, exciting, and sustainable ideas to life. In this position...
This position is responsible for the development and release of bulk materials, with a focus on 2K structural adhesives and foams, utilized in Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) Battery Pack. The engineer provides dedicated technical ownership of 2K adhesive and foam material specifications, supplier testing and data review, new test method development, adhesive dispensing process support, and initiate EHS/toxicological approval requests, and directly supports Ford’s battery manufacturing plant. Additionally, the materials engineer works with the vehicle teams and core engineering to resolve material compatibility, warranty, production, and processing problems encountered during the life of a components or assembly. The emphasis is on teamwork with Ford Product Development (PD) and Battery Manufacturing Engineering (BME), material suppliers, dispensing equipment suppliers, purchasing, laboratory engineers, other materials engineers, EHS/Industrial Hygiene, and manufacturing plant personnel.
What you'll do...
Demonstrate exemplary Ford OS behaviors – Excellence, Focus, and Collaboration
Develop and manage materials engineering foundation documents and update for prevent recurrence:
Material and Performance Specifications, Approved Source List and Ford Laboratory Test Methods, including 2K structural adhesive and foam material specifications
Support development material FEDE requirements and Design Rules
Ability to describe the operating environment in which the components/systems function.
Ability to describe the compatibility of the basic materials within the Ford manufacturing and processing environment including Tier 1 suppliers.

A plant supervisor today juggles several systems and side channels to run a shift. We are replacing that with InZone, the mobile app supervisors use to run a shift, which puts production status, issues, parts, and team chat in one place. Design for the plant floor: noise, gloves, poor connectivity, and shift hand-offs.

Show recommendations from ATP's AI agents with their sources and confidence.
Handle identity, permissions, and privacy for plant users.

Write tests, release through CI/CD, and monitor crashes and performance.
Fix issues fast and learn from how the app is really used.

A senior, hands-on technical leadership role. You will:
Lead multiple teams and their leaders across platform infrastructure, application platform, full-stack and AI engineering, release, security, and reliability.
Own the end-to-end CoreOS architecture and roadmap, partnering with a peer who owns industrial data and connectivity.
Turn plant software from a custom project per launch into a self-service platform that scales to every Ford plant.
You will lead that platform (runtime and edge, orchestration, application platform, fleet, security, and reliability) and the in-house applications and AI agents built on it. The guiding principles: plants keep running when the network or cloud is down; controllers keep real-time and safety control; OT/IT connections are secure and opened from OT outward; no traceability record is lost; people approve AI-recommended actions; everything is tested code; and what works in one plant reaches every plant by configuration.
What you'll do...
Lead the Organization
Hire and develop managers, technical leads, and engineers; build small, autonomous teams that ship often, own their services end to end, and spend time on the plant floor.
Set the engineering bar: design reviews and decision records, automated testing, everything as code, blameless post-incident reviews, and security by default.
Own roadmap, budget, and delivery against ATP lifecycle gates; make build, buy, and open-source decisions that avoid licensing lock-in; align partners across plants, controls, cybersecurity, IT, data, and AI, and report to executives.
Own the Platform Architecture and Runtime
Set the reference architecture across edge, plant, cloud, and cross-plant network (failure domains, high availability, control and data planes, layer contracts) and a standard plant blueprint so new lines and plants are stood up by configuration.
Deliver a hardened, immutable runtime that runs containerized workloads consistently on edge devices, plant clusters, and cloud, with local autonomy through outages and automatic reconciliation.
Build the secure cross-plant backbone with consistent compute, storage, identity, and policy everywhere.
Deliver Orchestration and the Application Platform
Build orchestration services that run plant workflows as durable, governed processes and bring brownfield systems on through adaptors.
Own the decision-to-action path: authorized, audited commands through platform APIs, with human approval where required and controllers keeping real-time control.
Provide self-service from code commit to running in a plant: versioned APIs and SDKs, templates, shared identity, and multi-tenancy, designed so engineers, AI agents, and coding agents reuse them without duplicate apps, APIs, or data stores.
Lead Application and AI Engineering
Lead full-stack teams building web and mobile plant applications (production, issues, quality, maintenance, parts) designed for noise, gloves, poor connectivity, and shift handoffs.
Set standards for AI agents that investigate issues and recommend actions, grounded in plant data, showing sources and confidence, and escalating to a person.
Build the shared AI foundation (model routing, secure agent interoperability, retrieval over plant knowledge, edge model serving) and make quality measurable through evaluation gates, tracing, and cost budgets.
Define how teams use AI coding agents, holding generated code to the same tests, review, security, and reuse checks as any code.
Scale, Secure, and Operate
Drive zero-touch provisioning and fleet management for thousands of edge devices, and one-click progressive rollout with signed artifacts, canary releases, and automated rollback around production schedules.
Own service levels, observability that never connects into OT, on-call, disaster recovery, and failure-injection testing.
Build in zero-trust identity, single sign-on, least privilege, OT/IT boundary controls, and IEC 62443 compliance.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer or Electrical Engineering, or related field.
12+ years in software, platform, or infrastructure engineering, building and operating large-scale distributed systems in production.
6+ years leading engineering organizations, including 3+ years leading managers or multiple teams.
Deep expertise in distributed systems and cloud-native platforms: container orchestration, event-driven architecture, replication and consensus, and designing for partial failure.
Track record building an internal platform adopted by multiple product teams, and leading teams that ship full-stack products at scale.
Hands-on understanding of production LLM systems: retrieval, tool use, agents, evaluation, and cost and latency trade-offs.
Hybrid edge-to-cloud operations across multiple sites: fleet management, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, progressive delivery, and SRE practice.
Strong security fundamentals (identity, PKI, zero trust, supply chain) and executive communication skills.

Manufacturing or IIoT experience: OT environments, Purdue model, ISA-95, IEC 62443, PLC, SCADA, and MES integration.
Edge computing in constrained or intermittently connected environments; control planes or workflow orchestration systems.
Multi-agent AI in production, retrieval and knowledge systems, and rolling out AI coding agents across an organization.

In this position...
Help Ford catch vehicle issues before customers do. As a Connected Vehicle Quality Engineer you'll use connected vehicle data and analytics to spot emerging diagnostic trends. You'll also lead cross-functional teams to resolve issues early, cutting costs and improving the ownership experience.
Join Ford Motor Company as a Connected Vehicle Quality Engineer for Early Warning and Detection, where you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality of customer vehicles. Based in Dearborn, Michigan, this hybrid role (4 days on-site, 1 day remote) leverages connected vehicle data and advanced analytics to identify Diagnostic Trouble Codes across critical subsystems, including Electronic Hardware Systems, Body Hardware and Software Controls Systems. You will lead cross-functional teams to resolve issues before they reach the customer, driving enterprise-wide initiatives to reduce costs and elevate the ownership experience.
As Ford continues its transformation into a digital-first automotive leader, the ability to monitor vehicle health through connected data is paramount. We are seeking a proactive Engineer/Project Manager to join our Digital Systems Quality organization, specifically focused on the high-stakes environment of customer vehicles. Our organization thrives on a culture of proactive discovery and rapid issue resolution.
What you'll do...
You will serve as a primary early warning system for the enterprise, transforming large-scale connected vehicle data into actionable insights to identify and address emerging Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) trends.
You will focus on the industry’s most complex domains — from the user experience of Electronic Hardware Systems, Body Hardware and Software Controls Systems.
Working primarily on-site at our Dearborn campus, you will lead cross-functional investigations, bringing together experts from Engineering, Manufacturing, and Service to solve complex problems at speed.
Extract and analyze information from connected vehicle data streams to identify early-stage DTCs and performance anomalies for post launch customer vehicles.
Lead specialized investigations into Electronic Hardware Systems, Body Hardware and Software Controls Systems performance, using domain knowledge to differentiate between software interactions, hardware failures, and calibration issues.
Manage cross-functional quality investigations, ensuring that emerging issues are tracked, root-caused, and resolved by the proper Product Development teams.
Strategic Reporting: Synthesize complex data into clear insights for leadership, focusing on the impact to enterprise Cost and Quality metrics.
Drive the development of automated detection tools and analytics dashboards to improve the "speed to detection" for vehicle health issues.

Experience applying structured problem-solving or root-cause methods to resolve technical, quality, reliability, or customer-impact issues.
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and driving alignment without direct authority.

Engineers across the company can go from idea to production through paved, self-service paths — without filing tickets for standard needs.

AI-assisted development is adopted broadly, safely, and measurably improves engineering throughput.

In this position...
Plant teams lose hours each shift piecing together what went wrong: pulling data from separate systems, chasing history, and rebuilding context before they can fix anything. That groundwork is the job of AIR (Agentic Issue Resolution), ATP's AI system that helps plant teams investigate and fix production issues. AI agents take an issue, gather approved evidence from plant systems, connect it to what the plant already knows, and recommend a fix that a person reviews and approves. Each confirmed fix is saved so the next plant can reuse it.
Why it's important...
AIR runs multiple investigation workflows on shared, reusable components.
Investigations use authorized evidence and produce traceable recommendations a person can review.
Plant teams spend less time rebuilding issue history and more time fixing problems.
A fix confirmed at one plant is reused at the next without rework.
The platform meets agreed security, reliability, and production-readiness standards.
What you'll do...
Design the AIR Platform
Define the architecture across user experience, workflow orchestration, agents, tools, knowledge, evaluation, and feedback.
Build reusable components for issue intake, investigation planning, evidence retrieval, analysis, recommendations, and follow-up.

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.
Product Creation and Industrialization (PC&I) brings together Ford’s vehicle, electric, digital and design teams with our global manufacturing system. Working as one end-to-end organization, we turn ideas into high-quality vehicles, software and experiences across gas, hybrid and electric, designed around what customers need.
In this position...
The Body Controls team is a growing team dedicated to creating Body Control Modules that integrate with existing architectures as well as our next-generation vehicle systems. Join our diverse team located in Dearborn; design and develop embedded software in the Body domain
What you'll do...
Diagnostic strategy and architecture : Define the diagnostic approach for assigned Body features and subsystems using systems engineering principles. Establish requirements, fault-detection coverage, DTC structure, and failure responses in alignment with the overall Body diagnostic architecture.
Standards alignment: Design diagnostic functionality to meet program requirements for UDS (ISO 14229), applicable OBD requirements, and corporate diagnostic standards. Coordinate with the broader diagnostics team to maintain consistent behavior across ECUs.
Diagnostic description integration : Integrate .cdd and .mdx diagnostic description files into the platform software configuration workflow. Check that service definitions, identifiers, data formats, and access conditions match the implemented software.
Diagnostic service implementation : Develop and configure diagnostic services, including Data Identifiers (DIDs), DTC reporting and clearing, RoutineControl, diagnostic sessions, and SecurityAccess (0x27). Implement service handlers, access checks, response timing, and negative-response handling.
Fault detection and DTC management : Define and implement fault-monitoring logic, detection thresholds, debounce criteria, enable conditions, and recovery behavior. Configure DTC mappings and associated diagnostic data according to feature requirements.
Middleware and application integration: Connect diagnostic platform middleware to application components through defined interfaces and callbacks. Integrate DID data access, routine execution, fault reporting, and application-specific service handling.
Diagnostic security integration: Work with platform security engineers to implement SecurityAccess (0x27), including the required security-level checks and seed/key interface. Validate authorized access, rejected requests, and unsuccessful access attempts against the platform requirements.
Validation and debugging: Develop and execute tests for diagnostic services, fault detection, DTC behavior, application interfaces, and failure responses. Verify behavior across supported sessions, security levels, operating conditions, and power cycles.
Production and service support : Resolve diagnostic issues identified during integration, vehicle testing, manufacturing, and service preparation. Support consistent diagnostic behavior across software releases.
Documentation and traceability: Maintain diagnostic requirements, service specifications, DTC definitions, interface documentation, and verification results. Track requirements and defects through implementation and closure.

2+ years of programming experience in C/C++ or Python (Candidates must have strong programming skills in C/C++, and be able to write highly portable and platform-agnostic code )
Experience with low level interfaces such as I2C, SPI, ICU, PWM, GPT and CAN

1+ years’ experience working in an agile environment

In our plants around the world, we’re constantly developing new technologies and processes to further increase our efficiency. You'll get the satisfaction of making great products people use and love.
In this position...
We are seeking a highly analytical and results-oriented Data Scientist with who can leveraging IIoT data from manufacturing environments to drive operational improvements and develop intelligent solutions. Proficient in the end-to-end data science lifecycle, from data ingestion (MQTT) and cloud-based processing (GCP) to advanced ML modeling (Python, SQL) and the development of interactive UIs and dashboards. Passionate about translating complex industrial data into actionable insights for smart factory initiatives.
What you’ll do…
Programming & Databases:
Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch, Dash/Streamlit, Flask/FastAPI)
SQL (Advanced querying, stored procedures, query optimization)
Cloud Platforms & Big Data:
Google Cloud Platform (GCP): BigQuery, Google Cloud Storage (GCS), Vertex AI, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, Dataproc
Data Technologies & Protocols:
MQTT, Data Pipelines (ETL/ELT), Data Cleaning & Preprocessing, Data Integration, Data Mining
Manufacturing & IIoT:
Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) Architectures & Principles
Rockwell Automation Ecosystem: ControlLogix, PLCs, VFDs, Studio 5000 (conceptual understanding)
Familiarity with software for data access/visualization tools
Manufacturing Environment & Equipment Data
Machine Learning & Statistical Analysis:
Quality Control/Prediction, Process Optimization
Time-Series Analysis, Classification, Regression, Clustering (e.g., OPTICS, DBSCAN)
Statistical Modeling, Hypothesis Testing
Visualization & UI/Dashboard Development:
Dashboarding Tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or Python libraries like Dash, Streamlit, Bokeh)
UI/UX Design Principles for Data Applications
Data Storytelling
Software Development & Operations:
Version Control (Git), Agile Methodologies, Basic API Development Responsibilities:
Develop and validate machine learning and statistical models to support business strategy.
Gather, manage, and analyze structured and unstructured data for reporting and analytics.
Research and apply innovative analytical methodologies and techniques.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define objectives and develop actionable insights.
Interpret and present analytical results
Create comprehensive reports, projections, and visual presentations.
Adhere to established guidelines and contribute to strategic discussions.
Required Skills:
Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field or 5+ years of experience in Data Science, IT, Statistics, or a related discipline.
Proficiency in tools and programming languages such as Python, R, SQL, or similar.
Expertise in machine learning techniques, including predictive modeling, clustering, and regression analysis is desirable.
Strong skills in handling structured and unstructured datasets for reporting and modeling.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.
Proven ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment on technical approaches.

• Strong written and verbal communication

Product Creation and Industrialization (PC&I) brings together Ford’s vehicle, electric, digital and design teams with our global manufacturing system. Working as one end-to-end organization, we turn ideas into high-quality vehicles, software and experiences across gas, hybrid and electric, designed around what customers need.
In this role...
This role is responsible for the development, maintenance, and production support of multiple highly critical cloud platform components within Ford’s Vehicle, Mobile and Cloud organization, specifically the Device Connectivity Platform. The position owns software delivery required to seamlessly integrate Ford’s Connectivity Platform as part of the Ford Partnership Alliance, supporting both Ford-engineered and Partner-engineered models.
The Cloud Software Engineering Director will help monitor cost and quality, support transformation efforts toward Ford’s Converged Connectivity strategy, and lead a sizable team through complex, high-visibility initiatives in an always-on connected vehicle environment. The role requires a strong combination of technical acumen, people leadership, collaboration, and the ability to make informed decisions across both technical implementation and broader product lifecycle direction.

Provide strategic and technical leadership for the development, maintenance, delivery, and production support of cloud platform software that enables Ford’s connected vehicle capabilities.
Own the technology strategy and software delivery required to integrate Ford’s connectivity platform with partner platforms across Ford-engineered and partner-engineered vehicle programs.
Set priorities and ensure predictable execution for business-critical platform capabilities operating in a global, always-on environment.
Establish performance objectives and drive measurable improvements in cost, quality, reliability, security, and delivery.

3+ years experience defining technology strategy, translating business objectives into executable roadmaps, and delivering business-critical software platforms at scale
Executive-level communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical topics into clear options, recommendations, risks, and decisions.
25% required travel to Europe, Asia/China, and other locations depending on vehicle program timelines.

Masters Degree

Do you believe a secure, reliable developer platform can help teams deliver better products, faster? Ford’s Marketing and Sales Technology organization depends on scalable cloud infrastructure, automated delivery, and strong platform engineering to support its eCommerce foundation. That’s where this role makes an impact.
We are seeking an experienced Platform Engineering Manager to lead the delivery and ongoing evolution of Ford’s Internal Developer Platform (IDP). You will guide the development of self-service capabilities for CI/CD automation, infrastructure provisioning, and platform orchestration, helping product teams improve their development experience and deliver software securely and efficiently.
This role combines platform engineering and cloud expertise with people leadership, delivery accountability, and cross-functional collaboration. You will partner with product teams, platform architects, Enterprise Architecture, IT Operations, security, SRE, and release-management teams to translate business needs into technical capabilities and measurable platform outcomes.
Platform Strategy, Roadmap & Delivery
Own and manage the Internal Developer Platform, including self-service services for CI/CD automation, infrastructure provisioning, and platform orchestration.
Lead delivery and evolution of next-generation platform capabilities in partnership with platform architects and technical teams.
Research existing and emerging technologies and recommend solutions that support future infrastructure and cloud-native workloads.
Evaluate tools and technologies for developing and deploying products on Ford’s eCommerce foundation layer.
Partner with product teams to understand developer challenges and prioritize platform capabilities that improve Developer Experience.
Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business needs into technical and non-functional specifications.
Work with senior leaders across Enterprise Architecture and IT Operations to deliver measurable improvements to the platform.
Team Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness
Lead, coach, and develop platform engineering team members, setting clear priorities, expectations, and accountability for delivery.
Mentor engineers to strengthen their technical capabilities and support their professional growth.
Build a collaborative, high-performing team focused on secure, reliable, and customer-centered platform services.
Foster knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution across the platform engineering organization.
Work effectively with global teams in remote and virtual environments.
Facilitate technical discussions across diverse perspectives and help teams reach decisions or recommendations.
Communicate effectively with executive leaders and stakeholders inside and outside the technology organization.
Lead teams through change and build trusted partnerships across cloud, security, SRE, release management, and software engineering.
Cloud Platform Engineering & DevSecOps
Design, develop, and maintain secure, scalable cloud infrastructure platforms using modern DevSecOps and platform engineering practices.
Manage platform services using Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Compute Engine, Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Operations suite, Anthos, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud Scheduler, Bigtable, AlloyDB, and other managed services.
Guide provisioning and management of cloud infrastructure, including VPCs, subnets, gateways, security groups, managed services, Kubernetes clusters, GKE, and Red Hat OpenShift.
Lead Infrastructure as Code reviews and the automation and deployment of cloud infrastructure.
Guide automation using tools such as Terraform, Packer, Ansible, shell scripting, NX Cloud, Helm, and Argo CD.
Manage and improve CI/CD capabilities using tools such as Tekton, GitHub Actions, and Jenkins.
Establish and implement best practices for code quality, security, performance, and scalability using tools such as SonarQube, Cycode, 42Crunch, Astra, JFrog Xray, build-time container vulnerability scanning, and FOSSA.
Build automation for repeatable DevSecOps tasks and connect CI/CD with infrastructure services to improve software engineering productivity.
Reliability, Security & Observability
Lead adoption of DevSecOps, observability, and platform engineering practices across the organization.
Oversee patch management and use monitoring and APM tools such as Dynatrace, AppDynamics, Prometheus, Grafana, and ELK to support platform health and alerting.
Guide implementation and management of auto-scaling, high availability, disaster recovery, and multi-region Active/Active and Active/Passive architectures.
Apply cloud-native practices to support scalable, reliable, and available platform services.
Partner with technical teams to address security, performance, and operational concerns across the platform.
Manage Cloud FinOps practices to monitor and optimize cloud infrastructure consumption costs.
Transformation, Innovation & Continuous Improvement
Advance Shift Left practices for quality, security, and open-source software, alongside Shift Right platform engineering practices.
Support adoption of AI-enabled automation and AIOps to improve platform operations and Developer Experience.
Guide the deployment, evaluation, and monitoring of AI agents used for platform engineering service automation.
Use platform, delivery, reliability, and cost insights to identify improvements and inform platform priorities.
Promote cloud-native development and platform practices across Ford’s Marketing and Sales Technology organization.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline—or equivalent relevant experience.
Preferred degree: Bachelor of Engineering.
Experience
12+ years of relevant professional experience.
Experience developing and maintaining self-service platform products for CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, cloud services, and observability.
Experience leading platform engineering delivery, cloud infrastructure initiatives, or DevSecOps adoption.
Experience managing or operating services on GCP and supporting cloud-native application development.
Experience with team leadership, mentoring, technical delivery, and coordinating across multiple stakeholder groups.
Experience working with product teams to understand requirements and improve developer productivity and experience.
Experience driving high availability, disaster recovery, auto-scaling, and multi-region platform practices.
Experience partnering with cloud, security, SRE, and release-management teams.
Strong communication, interpersonal, facilitation, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to work effectively with executive leadership and global teams.
Required Technical Experience
Experience developing and maintaining self-service platform products for CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, cloud services, and observability.
Strong experience with GCP services, including Compute Engine, Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Operations suite, Anthos, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud Scheduler, Bigtable, AlloyDB, and other managed services.

Working knowledge of microservices frameworks such as Spring Boot or Micronaut.
Experience building scalable, reliable, and available cloud-native or transactional systems, including multi-tenant environments.
Strong engineering and delivery background, with the ability to guide technical talent on quality and delivery practices.

Expertise with patch management and observability/APM tools such as Dynatrace, AppDynamics, Prometheus, Grafana, or ELK.

About the Organization
We are undergoing a historic industrial shift—moving from building great vehicles to building the sophisticated, scalable systems that power them. The Advanced Industrial Technology organization was created to operationalize this shift. Our mission is not to deploy isolated tools; it is to build an ecosystem that learns from factory data, transforms it into scalable platforms, and delivers measurable enterprise value.
This organization is designed to position us as a leader in industrial innovation. We accelerate digital evolution and manufacturing excellence by integrating cutting-edge technology directly into our global operations. Our structure includes vertical business units focused on specific technology stacks, supported by shared services that ensure scale and operational consistency.
As part of this team, the Sight Vertical is responsible for building an end-to-end business around AI/ML anomaly detection products using both image data ( Vision ) and parametric data ( Sense ). This vertical transforms raw data into actionable manufacturing intelligence through products focused on visual error-proofing, defect detection, and assembly process monitoring.
The Position
Reporting to the Sight | Vision Product Family Manager, the Software Engineering Manager is responsible for the execution and technical health of the Vision product lines. You will lead the engineering team in translating strategic goals into robust, scalable software, ensuring our products meet rigorous industrial standards for global rollout.
What You’ll Be Able to Do
Engineering Leadership & Mentorship: Lead, coach, and grow a multi-disciplinary team of software and data engineers. Foster a collaborative environment focused on continuous improvement and professional development.
Technical Delivery: Own the software development lifecycle for Sight Vision products. Ensure the team delivers high-quality, maintainable code that meets project milestones and performance benchmarks and results in a reliable and highly scalable product.
Architecture & Strategy: Provide technical oversight for software and hardware architecture, MLOps pipelines, technology stack selection, and controls integration. Balance the need for rapid innovation with the stability required for 24/7 manufacturing environments.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Product Managers and stakeholders to translate manufacturing challenges into technical roadmaps and executable engineering backlogs.
Platform Integration: Ensure all vision products are built for seamless integration with centralized data and operating platforms, adhering to a "build once, scale everywhere" philosophy.
Operational Excellence: Drive engineering best practices, including automated testing, CI/CD, and robust monitoring for models deployed at the "edge" (on-site factory hardware).
Innovation: Drive innovation by integrating Agentic workflows and AI-assisted engineering tools to maximize team productivity and software quality
Deployment Oversight: Work with site-level stakeholders to ensure technical solutions account for real-world variables such as factory lighting, line speeds, and network constraints.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or a related technical field.
Leadership Experience: 5+ years of experience directly managing software engineering teams, with a proven track record of hiring, mentoring, and retaining talent.
Technical Background: 8+ years of experience in software engineering, Computer Vision, or complex data-driven products.
Systems Knowledge: Deep understanding of the machine learning lifecycle (data engineering, model training, inference, and monitoring).
Agile Proficiency: Extensive experience leading teams in Agile environments, managing sprints, and optimizing delivery velocity.
Preferred Requirements
Master’s in a technical field related to Computer Vision, Software Development, or Data Science.
Experience with MLOps platforms and cloud infrastructure (GCP).
Experience scaling software products from a single pilot to a global enterprise footprint in an industrial or IoT context.

ford-70616.text:
Join the Global Dev Tools team within the Enterprise Platform Engineering and Operations (EPEO) organization to build and operate the cloud-native platform that powers Ford's Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). As a Senior DevOps Engineer, you will play a hands-on, technical role in enabling Product Development Office (PDO) teams. You will design, build, and operate the infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and automation that let engineering teams ship reliably and often.
Your work will center around Ford's core tech stack, featuring Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Azure for cloud infrastructure, and GitHub Enterprise with GitHub Actions and Jenkins for CI/CD. Infrastructure is fully codified with Terraform, with GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) self-hosted runners deployed on Kubernetes (GKE) to power scalable, on-demand CI/CD. You'll support Actions workflows that build and deploy Java (Spring Boot), Go, and Python applications, orchestrate AI agents to automate operational toil, lead technical evaluations of emerging AI developer and infrastructure tools, and ensure all platform systems meet Ford's stringent performance, security, and scalability benchmarks.
Build the platform. Use Terraform to provision and manage GCP infrastructure — GKE clusters, VMs, storage buckets, networking, and other resources as the platform grows — with Config Sync driving GitOps-style deployment of the GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) and other workloads onto GKE. Lay the foundation for expanding into additional GCP services (Cloud Run, Compute Engine, Cloud Functions, IAM) and Azure as platform needs evolve.
Core scripting, config, and version control. Write and maintain YAML for pipeline definitions, Kubernetes manifests, and GitOps configs; use Git and GitHub Enterprise fluently for branching, PR workflows, and repository management; script in Bash/Shell (in addition to Python/Go) to glue together automation, tooling, and day-to-day operational tasks.
Automate everything that shouldn't be manual. Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform), self-service pipelines, auto-remediation. If a human repeats it, write the code — or point an agent at it — to stop it.
Own CI/CD end to end. Design, develop, and optimize robust, automated GitHub Actions workflows and Jenkins pipelines that package, test, and deploy software platform utilities. Support workflows that build and deploy Java (Spring Boot), Go, and Python applications, letting engineers ship multiple times a day with confidence.
API & Backend Integration. Design, develop, and secure backend APIs and integrations using Java (Spring Boot), Go, or Python; integrate with enterprise API gateways (Apigee) using OAuth2 and JWT, and support API lifecycle management across platform tooling.
Run containers and orchestration in production. Build, secure, and operate container images with Docker and/or Podman, and run them at scale on Kubernetes (GKE) — including the parts that break: crash loops, resource contention, networking edge cases, and noisy-neighbor problems. Bring the operational maturity to diagnose and fix these fast, and to harden the platform against recurrence.
Engineer reliability and observability in. SLOs, monitoring, alerting that means something, and incident response that gets calmer every quarter. Leverage GCP BigQuery and Data Studio (Looker Studio) to build observability and platform-health dashboards that surface real signal to stakeholders. Make on-call boring.
Own incident response. Bring a strong troubleshooting mindset to production issues — diagnose root cause quickly under pressure, drive incidents to resolution, and turn each one into a lasting fix rather than a repeat page.

Our advanced energy team is a dynamic division dedicated to powering the future through advanced electric vehicle (EV) battery systems and related electrified energy solutions. As we scale these advanced electrification initiatives, we are seeking technically strong engineers who can help establish the foundation for our product execution, safety strategy, and vehicle readiness.
In this position
The Battery Management Controls Software Engineer develops the application-layer control software that determines how a high-voltage battery system behaves: operating states, high-voltage sequencing, protection, limits, thermal control, diagnostics, and coordination across multiple strings.
Assignments may include supervisory system-level control software or string-level control software and may shift across the product architecture over the life of the program.
The ideal candidate has designed state machines, protection strategy, and diagnostic logic on a production program, works fluently in a model-based development environment with production code generation, and is comfortable debugging control behavior on real hardware.
What you'll do...
Develop and own operating state machines and mode management, including supervisory coordination across multiple controllers.
Implement high-voltage sequencing: precharge control and completion verification, contactor activation and deactivation, contactor diagnostics including welded and open contact detection, and interlock handling.
Implement protection strategy: cell and pack overvoltage and undervoltage, overcurrent, overtemperature and undertemperature, isolation loss, and thermal event detection and response.
Implement current and power limit calculation and arbitration, including derate strategy and coordination of limits across levels of the system.
Implement cell balancing demand logic and coordinate balancing behavior across modules and strings.
Implement thermal management control, including actuation, setpoint strategy, and thermal diagnostics.
Implement aggregation and consolidation of measured and estimated states for reporting at system level, and fault propagation and annunciation to external systems.
Own diagnostic strategy: fault detection, debounce, classification, storage, clearing, and reporting.
Integrate and calibrate estimation models delivered by algorithm engineering; own the calibration parameter set and its documentation.
Develop application software using model-based development with production code generation, plus hand-written C where appropriate.
Author software requirements and design documentation traceable to system requirements; support safety and security analyses.
Support validation debug, root cause analysis, and field issue resolution.
You'll have...
Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Computer, Mechatronics, Controls, or Mechanical Engineering.
5+ years developing embedded application or control software for electronic control units.
Model-based development proficiency with production code generation, plus working C ability.
Demonstrated state machine, sequencing, and diagnostic strategy design on a production program.
Requirements-driven software development with traceability, unit testing, and code review discipline.
Comfort working directly with hardware, benches, and instrumentation to debug control behavior.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability and willingness to travel occasionally.
Even better, you may have...
Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls, or a related technical field.
Battery management control software: contactor sequencing, protection strategy, limit calculation, and balancing.
High-voltage system experience and understanding of isolation, precharge, and interlock principles.
Software development under functional safety process requirements, including safety mechanism implementation.
Calibration methodology and parameter management for production programs.
Coordination or aggregation logic across distributed controllers.
Thermal management control strategy experience.
Technical Skills
Model-based development and production code generation
Embedded C application software
State machine and mode management design
High-voltage sequencing and contactor control
Protection strategy and limit arbitration
Diagnostic strategy design
Thermal control strategy
Balancing demand logic
Calibration and parameter management

Modern Tech Stack & Best Practices: We are a team that believes in doing things the right way. We champion Test-Driven Development (TDD), clean code, robust CI/CD pipelines, and microservices architecture.

Collaborate & Influence: Partner closely with Product Managers and UI/UX Designers to translate complex fleet management needs into elegant, developer-friendly APIs (OAS standards).

Mentor & Lead: Help elevate the team's technical capabilities by conducting thoughtful code reviews, sharing architectural best practices, and onboarding newer team members.

6+ years of experience within the Spring Ecosystem (Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Data).
6+ years of strong expertise in relational databases, specifically PostgreSQL or similar SQL databases, including query optimization and schema design.
6+ years of deploying systems to the cloud (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and a passion for automation, robust CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code.
6+ of being a strong advocate for Agile methodologies, TDD, and collaborative development.

Experience with Event-Driven Architectures and messaging systems (Pub/Sub, Kafka, or RabbitMQ).

As a Software Developer in Test, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining automated tests for our embedded software products.
You will also be responsible for defining, decomposing, and realizing feature, function, interface, and testing requirements and associated integration efforts for Ford’s next-generation electronic systems and controls.
You will lead the end-to-end integration and testing of these systems, collaborating with cross-functional teams to support product design, vehicle behavior definition, prototype bring-up, and debugging.

- Design, build, and maintain comprehensive automotive system-level test benches, ensuring their seamless integration of hardware and software components for reliable and scalable test environments, with a strong emphasis on Python-driven automation.
- Develop comprehensive verification and validation plans, test plans, test cases, and test scripts to rigorously validate functional, non-functional, performance, safety, and regression aspects of automotive software systems and components.
- Overseeing and coordinating the development and validation of Distributed (e.g. Software, Electrical & Mechanical) Features on all UEV programs.
- Collaborate extensively with cross-functional teams, including software developers (e.g. UX, HMI, Connectivity), controls engineers, and systems engineers, to:
o Develop item definition, identify the system goal, create technical requirements and test scenarios as per consumer electronics and automotive standards
o Authoring and releasing Core Feature Requirements and Specification documents (JAMA, FEDE and JIRA)
o Develop feature specifications, Quality documents (Quality History, Parameter Diagram, Feature Failure Mode Avoidance (FMEA) documentation), feature verification plan, etc.
o Review existing system designs to find new opportunities for cost or quality improvement, with a keen focus on the end customer’s user experience.
o Interact with hardware and software teams to come up with specification development for must have products, collaborating with device owners, program teams, core engineers and functional areas to create balanced solutions to competing requirements.
o Execute test cases and test scripts, leveraging advanced Python automation to enhance testing efficiency, accuracy, and repeatability across various testing phases.
o Decompose functional and non-functional requirements to comprehensive test scenarios that are actionable against V&V test platforms and test infrastructure.
o Create a constant feedback loop between field issues and functional requirements and test cases, ensuring that we are left-shifting testing and defect detection.
You'll have...
- Bachelor's, Master’s, or PhD degree in Electrical/Mechatronics Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
- 5+ years of experience in software testing, preferably with embedded systems in the automotive industry.
- Strong programming skills in Python, Rust, or other relevant languages used in embedded software development and verification.
- Experience writing automated tests in test frameworks such as Pytest, Slash, Robot Framework, or similar.
- Strong understanding of electrical engineering fundamentals and ability to apply them to automotive concepts
- Experience with requirements capture in requirements management software platforms (JAMA, Polarion, DOORs, etc.)
- Strong experience debugging embedded systems at a module and/or system level, and the ability to triage nightly regression failures.
- Experience with software testing tools, frameworks, and methodologies (e.g., requirements-driven test development, unit testing, integration testing, system testing, automated testing).
- Experience designing/integrating/validating embedded software features across one or more of the following domains: network communication, cloud and connectivity, multimedia, infotainment, Android/iOS, and low-voltage power distribution.
- A systems approach to design and development, with an eagerness for continuous improvement and collaborative, cross-functional teamwork in a dynamic environment.
- Excellent teamwork, problem-solving, communication, and project management skills

- Electrical Systems Engineering experience including understanding of systems engineering V model
- Experience with Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA).
- Familiarity with common electronic components and comfort reading circuit design schematics & data sheets
- Ability to work independently on technical tasks, effective troubleshooting, and problem-solving with minimal supervision.

Who You Are
A software engineer who chose infrastructure. You write real code — not just glue scripts. You'd be dangerous on a product team, but you'd rather build the systems that make every product team faster. Platforms, not tickets.
An agent orchestrator, not a typist. You don't want to be a faster keyboard. You manage agents to do the heavy lifting — generating IaC, triaging alerts, writing the first draft of the runbook — while you keep your hands on the architecture and the judgment calls. The terminal is a cockpit for orchestration.
Productively lazy. Your instinct is to eliminate toil at the root. If a human is clicking through a console or babysitting a deploy, you replace them with code or an agent. Your biggest bottleneck should be deciding what to automate next — while the automation runs itself.
Fundamentals first. Linux, networking, distributed systems, how things actually fail under load. You understand the machine, not just the tool that wraps it. When the pipeline breaks at 2am, you can read the trace and fix the cause — and when an agent proposes a fix, you can tell whether it's right.
First-principles thinker with vision. You design for the failure mode, not the happy path. You question the assumptions, simplify the system, and build for the next order of magnitude — not just today's load.
High agency. You don't wait for perfect specs or permission. You find a path, propose it, and move. Large organizations have walls; you figure out which ones to go through, around, or remove — and you do it constructively.

Build the platform. Design and operate the cloud-native foundation on GCP — compute, networking, observability, and the golden paths other teams build on.
Automate everything that shouldn't be manual. Infrastructure-as-code, self-service pipelines, auto-remediation. If a human repeats it, you write the code — or point an agent at it — to stop it.
Orchestrate agents for ops. Use AI to draft IaC, generate tests, triage incidents, and summarize signal from noise. You direct, review, and harden — agents do the grunt work.
Own CI/CD end to end. Fast, reliable, reproducible delivery. Build the pipelines that let engineers ship multiple times a day with confidence.
Engineer reliability in. SLOs, monitoring, alerting that means something, and incident response that gets calmer every quarter. Make on-call boring.
Secure the path. Bake security and compliance into the platform so doing the right thing is the easy thing — secrets management, least privilege, supply-chain hygiene.
Support AI workloads. Build the infrastructure that runs LLM and agentic systems in production — scaling, cost control, and the deployment patterns AI apps actually need.

A real programming language, deep — Python and/or Go preferred. You write production code, not just YAML.
GCP — Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Functions, networking, IAM. Designed, deployed, and operated at scale.
IaC & CI/CD — Terraform, Cloud Build, GitHub Actions, or equivalent. Reproducible, version-controlled, peer-reviewed infrastructure.
Containers & orchestration — Docker and Kubernetes in production, including the parts that break.
Observability — metrics, logs, tracing. You can find the needle, not just collect haystacks.
AI-assisted development — fluent with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows, and clear-eyed about where they help and where they don't.
AI workload experience — bonus for running LLM/agentic systems, GPUs, or model-serving infrastructure in production.
Reliability & security fundamentals — SLOs, incident response, and security-by-default in pipelines.
Requirements
BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. MS is a plus, not a substitute for shipping software.
3+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering — with real software engineering, not just configuration.
2+ years on cloud-native platforms (GCP preferred), operating production systems.
Demonstrable automation you've built — show us the toil you killed, not the tools you've read about.

You will join the Digital Cabin organization as the dedicated Data Scientist for our next-generation AI Digital Assistant. This AI-driven feature is live on mobile and rapidly expanding into our In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI) systems to answer questions, execute tasks, provide vehicle reports, and enhance the driving experience.
This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the data strategy for a high-priority AI product from the ground up. As a hands-on individual contributor, you'll build the analytics foundation and dashboards the product team relies on, and lead the evaluation work that answers the harder questions: Is the assistant giving good answers and completing tasks successfully? How do we know our measurements are right? And what is it worth to the business?
What you'll do…
AI Response & Task Evaluation: Design methodologies to evaluate both informational responses (accuracy, grounding, helpfulness) and task completion (did the assistant understand the request, take the right action, and finish the job, including across multi-turn conversations). Build ground-truth evaluation sets from real conversations, keep development and held -out test sets separate, and run regression checks on every prompt and model update.
Validate the Evaluation: Calibrate automated scoring, including LLM-as-judge, against human review, and confirm offline scores match real user behavior such as retries and abandoned sessions. When they disagree, fix the evaluation rather than defend the score.
NLP & Utterance Analysis: Cluster and categorize raw user utterances to build an intent taxonomy from what users actually say . Perform sentiment and failure analysis to surface actionable product insights.
Business Impact: Analyze how the assistant relates to outcomes such as warranty claims, support contacts, and connectivity subscription conversion, using methods that account for selection bias so leadership gets credible estimates, not misleading correlations.
Data Integration & Sanitization: Work directly in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to join and structure mobile, vehicle, customer support, warranty, and subscription data into robust analytical datasets, ensuring strict adherence to data privacy and PII handling standards.
Problem Framing & Metric Definition: Act as a strategic partner to Product Managers. Challenge assumptions and define core conversational metrics (e.g., task success rate, containment, support deflection).
Dashboards & Self-Service: Build and maintain narrative-driven dashboards in Looker and/or Power BI that empower the product team to answer their own day-to-day questions.
Bridge the Mobile-to-IVI Gap: Act as the analytical bridge as the assistant expands from the Ford app into the vehicle, standardizing mobile data against emerging in-vehicle data contracts and partnering with instrumentation teams on what gets logged.
You'll have…
Education: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or technical field (e.g., Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering).
Experience: 5+ years in Data Science, Product Analytics, or Applied Machine Learning.
LLM Evaluation: Hands-on experience evaluating LLM or conversational AI output in a real application, including building labeled evaluation datasets, separating development and test sets, LLM-as-judge or rubric-based scoring validated against human review, and hallucination tracking.
Applied NLP: Proficiency in Python or R applying NLP, clustering, and classification to real-world unstructured text.
SQL: Highly proficient in complex SQL (window functions, CTEs, JSON/nested data) to structure datasets independently.
Dashboards: Experience building dashboards for non-technical stakeholders in Looker, Power BI, or similar tools.
"Full-Stack" Capability: Demonstrated ability to go from raw data to model to business insight without relying on a central data team for every step.
Analytics as Code: Experience with version control (e.g., Git/GitHub) and peer-reviewed analytics workflows.
Even better, you may have…
Master's or PhD in a quantitative or technical field.
Experience evaluating task-oriented or agentic AI systems (tool calling, multi-turn task completion).
Conversational AI, voice assistant, or chatbot experience in a consumer product.
Causal inference with observational data to estimate business impact.
Designing and analyzing A/B tests in a product environment.
GCP experience, especially BigQuery , and Looker semantic layers ( LookML ).
Behavioral analytics (e.g., Amplitude) or data modeling with dbt .
Automotive, connected vehicle, warranty, or subscription analytics experience.

In this position...
This is an opportunity to work in a research environment defining the next generation of emissions and aftertreatment simulation. As diesel and gas powertrains evolve toward hybridization and electrification, the underlying simulation infrastructure must be reinvented to keep pace. In this role, you will research and build the simulation architectures needed to integrate models of fundamentally new system concepts — including hybridized gas/diesel emissions controls and electrified aftertreatment components such as electric DPFs and electrically heated catalysts — well before they exist in any production toolchain.
What you'll do...
You will work alongside teams developing engine, combustion, aftertreatment, and controls models, with a focus on exploring how these models can be connected, represented, and evolved to support technologies that don't yet have established simulation methods. On a three to five year research horizon, you will also investigate how Agentic AI can be embedded directly into the simulation pipeline — to automate model calibration, accelerate integration, and fundamentally change the speed and quality of simulation.
This role is suited for someone who wants to operate at the leading edge of simulation research, prototyping new approaches and helping define the roadmap.
Research: Next-Generation Simulation Architecture:
Research and prototype simulation architectures capable of integrating models for hybridized gas/diesel emissions control systems, enabling early-stage development and analysis of concepts ahead of production readiness.
Develop and integrate models for electrified aftertreatment components — electric DPFs, electrically heated catalysts, and other emerging technologies — in close collaboration with hardware, combustion, and controls research teams.
Explore new co-simulation and model-integration methods needed to combine models across teams, tools, and fidelity levels for these next-generation systems, where standard interfaces and workflows may not yet exist.
Build proof-of-concept integration frameworks and demonstrate feasibility before handoff toward broader adoption.
Research: Agentic AI in the Simulation Pipeline:
Investigate and prototype the application of Agentic AI within the simulation pipeline — for example, automated model calibration, intelligent scenario/test generation, self-diagnosing integration issues, or AI-assisted model reduction — on a 3–5 year roadmap.
Evaluate emerging AI/ML and simulation tools and methodologies, assess their applicability to emissions and aftertreatment simulation, and build early demonstrations of value.
Partner with technical leadership to help shape the long-term research roadmap for simulation of electrified and hybridized emissions systems.
Supporting Collaboration:
Engage with teams building engine, emissions, and aftertreatment models (using GT-Power, WAVE-RT, and in-house tools) to understand existing modeling approaches and identify where next-generation architectures can build on or diverge from them.
Document research findings, architectural concepts, and prototype results to inform future integration efforts.

Master's degree in Mechanical / Chemical / Automotive / Controls Engineering or a related field

Experience developing or integrating physics-based models of combustion, emissions, or aftertreatment systems
Programming background in Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or C/C++
Demonstrated ability to research, prototype, and independently drive open-ended technical problems to a working solution
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document and present research findings to technical and non-technical audiences
