We are seeking a Threat & Vulnerability Management (TVM) Security Engineer (GSR Level) to help strengthen Ford’s cybersecurity posture through the identification, analysis, prioritization, remediation, and reporting of security vulnerabilities across enterprise, product, manufacturing, and customer-facing environments.
This role will partner closely with Security Operations, Infrastructure, Cloud, Product Cybersecurity, Manufacturing, Engineering, and external service providers to drive a risk-based vulnerability management program. The TVM Security Engineer will help ensure vulnerabilities are identified quickly, assessed accurately, remediated effectively, and communicated clearly to reduce cyber risk across the organization.
What you'll do...
Vulnerability Management Operations: Execute and support vulnerability scanning, assessment, validation, prioritization, remediation tracking, and reporting across enterprise, cloud, endpoint, product, manufacturing, and customer-facing environments.
Risk-Based Prioritization: Analyze vulnerabilities using technical severity, exploitability, threat intelligence, asset criticality, business impact, exposure, and compensating controls to identify and prioritize the most significant risks.
Scanning & Assessment: Configure, maintain, and optimize vulnerability scanning technologies, asset discovery capabilities, authenticated scanning, and assessment schedules to improve security coverage and data quality.
Remediation Coordination: Partner with infrastructure, engineering, product, manufacturing, and application teams to communicate findings, establish remediation plans, track progress, validate fixes, and manage risk acceptance or exception processes.
Threat Intelligence Integration: Incorporate threat intelligence, active exploitation information, attacker techniques, and emerging vulnerabilities into prioritization and response activities.
Vulnerability Verification: Perform technical validation of vulnerability findings, evaluate false positives, verify remediation, and assess the effectiveness of compensating controls.
Security Operations Collaboration: Work closely with Security Operations and Incident Response teams to identify vulnerabilities associated with active threats, security incidents, suspicious activity, and known attacker tactics.
Product, Customer & Connected Environment Support: Support vulnerability management processes for connected products, customer-facing systems, and related technology environments in coordination with product cybersecurity and engineering teams.
Manufacturing & Operational Technology Security: Assist with vulnerability assessment, remediation planning, and risk management activities for manufacturing and operational technology environments while accounting for operational availability and safety requirements.
Compliance & Regulatory Support: Support vulnerability management evidence, reporting, remediation tracking, and operational control requirements aligned with applicable cybersecurity standards, internal policies, regulatory obligations, and NERC CIP requirements.
Metrics & Reporting: Develop and maintain dashboards, metrics, and reports related to vulnerability exposure, remediation performance, asset coverage, overdue findings, exception status, and overall risk trends.
Program Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve scanning coverage, asset inventory quality, remediation workflows, automation, vulnerability data integration, and stakeholder engagement.
Documentation & Governance: Create and maintain vulnerability management procedures, technical standards, remediation guidance, exception documentation, and stakeholder communications.
You'll have...
Required:
Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in vulnerability management, cybersecurity engineering, security operations, cloud security, infrastructure security, or a related technical cybersecurity role.
Vulnerability Management: Hands-on experience conducting, interpreting, prioritizing, and validating vulnerability assessments across endpoint, server, network, cloud, application, or container environments.
Risk Assessment: Experience applying risk-based approaches to vulnerability prioritization using factors such as CVSS, exploitability, asset criticality, threat intelligence, business impact, and exposure.
Remediation Management: Experience partnering with technical teams to communicate vulnerability findings, coordinate remediation, validate corrective actions, and manage risk exceptions.
Technical Knowledge: Working knowledge of common vulnerability classes, secure configuration practices, patch management, endpoint security, network security, cloud security, identity and access management, and application security concepts.
Security Tools: Experience using vulnerability management, asset discovery, security analytics, endpoint management, or configuration assessment platforms.
Scripting & Automation: Familiarity with scripting or automation languages such as Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar technologies.
Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical vulnerabilities, business risk, and remediation requirements to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent related work experience.
Even better, you may have...
Preferred:
Experience with vulnerability management and security platforms such as Tanium, Elastic, Jira Service Management, Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Wiz, or similar technologies.
Experience integrating vulnerability findings with ticketing, asset management, configuration management, security information and event management, or security orchestration platforms.
Experience with cloud vulnerability management, container security, infrastructure-as-code security, DevSecOps, or application security testing.
Experience supporting vulnerability management activities across manufacturing, operational technology, industrial control systems, energy, automotive, or other highly regulated environments.
Familiarity with vulnerability management and remediation requirements associated with NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-40, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-82, ISO 27001, IEC 62443, NERC CIP, or similar standards.
Experience using threat intelligence, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, exploit data, and attacker activity to prioritize remediation efforts.
Industry certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CySA+, CISSP, CISM, GIAC GCIH, GIAC GSEC, AWS Certified Security – Specialty, Microsoft Azure Security Engineer, or equivalent.

This leader will shape the strategy, engineering, and operations of Ford's Identity and Access Management platform across workforce, dealer, supplier, customer, workload, and emerging AI agent identities.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Global Head of Identity and Access Management , this role begins as a highly strategic individual contributor with broad enterprise influence and an expectation to build and lead a global platform engineering team.
This is a unique opportunity to secure and enable every interaction across employees, dealers, suppliers, customers, applications, workloads, connected vehicles, and AI-powered systems.

Shape Ford's Identity Strategy
Define and execute Ford's enterprise Identity and Access Management strategy and multi-year roadmap.
Establish identity as a foundational platform that enables business growth, customer experiences, and digital innovation.
Drive Zero Trust adoption across workforce, dealer, supplier, customer, workload, and AI agent ecosystems.
Partner with cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, and technology leaders to strengthen enterprise resilience through identity-centric controls.
Influence the future of identity security across Entra ID, Google Cloud Platform, and emerging cloud-native identity architectures.
Lead AI-Powered Identity Innovation
Define Ford's approach to securing AI agents, autonomous systems, and machine-to-machine identities.
Implement AI-assisted identity lifecycle management, access governance, certification campaigns, and risk-based decisioning.
Drive adoption of AI-enabled engineering practices including code generation, automated testing, vulnerability remediation, and intelligent observability.
Establish governance frameworks that enable responsible and secure use of AI across identity platforms.
Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve self-service experiences through intelligent automation.
Build and Modernize Identity Platforms
Lead modernization of Ford's identity platforms using cloud-native architectures, APIs, automation, and platform engineering practices.
Manage engineering team responsible for 24/7 global operations for various Identity and Access Management Platforms and Products delivering always on customer experiences.
Deliver secure, scalable, and highly available identity services for employees, partners, suppliers, dealers, and customers.
Drive Site Reliability Engineering practices focused on resiliency, observability, availability, and operational excellence.
Improve engineering velocity through automation, Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, and AI-assisted development workflows.
Partner across enterprise technology teams to integrate identity capabilities into Ford's digital platforms.
Build High-Performing Teams
Recruit, develop, and mentor world-class engineers, architects, and technical leaders.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Communicate strategy, outcomes, risks, and opportunities to executive leadership.
Build strong relationships across business, security, compliance, and technology organizations.
Lead through complexity while maintaining focus on measurable business outcomes.

10+ years of experience designing, building, or leading enterprise-scale Identity and Access Management platforms.

Deep expertise across multiple identity disciplines including:
Identity Governance & Administration (IGA)
Customer Identity & Access Management (CIAM)
Privileged Access Management (PAM)
Authentication & Federation
Workload Identity & Agent Identity
Access Management
Experience leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs.
Strong understanding of Zero Trust architecture and modern identity security principles.
Expertise with modern identity standards including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, FIDO2, SAML, SPIFFE, Cedar, OPA, AuthZEN, or related technologies.
Experience leveraging AI and automation to improve engineering, operations, and security outcomes.

In this position...
The Product Analyst serves as the program’s regulatory and market radar, translating state-specific regulatory requirements, filing activity, connected-data obligations, and competitive intelligence into decision-ready product insights.
The role supports the Underwriting Manager and works across Ford Pro Insure, the Master MGA, and internal control functions to help keep the product roadmap compliant, commercially competitive, and operationally ready for current and prospective jurisdictions.
Function: The research and product-intelligence partner that connects product strategy with state regulatory, filing, data, and market realities.
The Product Analyst’s primary function is to evaluate regulatory, market, and product evidence; identify implications for forms, rules, telematics features, and state expansion; and communicate clear recommendations to accountable decisionmakers.
The position researches, reviews, coordinates, and recommends. Formal legal interpretation, actuarial judgment, filing submission, compliance approval, and state-entry authorization remain with designated Ford, carrier, MGA, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, and Actuarial owners.
What you'll do...
Regulatory Intelligence
•Legislative and Regulatory Monitoring: Tracks relevant state bills, Department of Insurance bulletins, statutory amendments, and other developments affecting commercial auto insurance, including changes to minimum liability limits and telematics or usage-based insurance requirements.
• Business Impact Analysis: Summarizes changes in clear business terms, including effective dates, affected products or jurisdictions, potential operational impact, and actions that may be needed.
• Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinates follow-up with Compliance, Legal, Actuarial, Claims, Marketing, Underwriting, Product, and the Master MGA; maintains source references and an auditable regulatory change log.
• Escalation Support: Escalates material regulatory changes, open questions, and decision needs to designated owners in a timely manner.
Market Entry Analysis
• State Profiles and Readiness Assessments: Prepares evidence-based state profiles covering commercial auto requirements, filing and approval processes, mandatory coverages, minimum limits, market conditions, and anticipated filing lead times.
• Entry Barrier Assessment: Identifies state-specific product deviations, telematics restrictions, system needs, claims considerations, resource dependencies, and other launch barriers.
• Roadmap and Launch Support: Partners with the Underwriting Manager and Master MGA to translate market priorities into a sequenced rollout plan with realistic timeline assumptions and launch-gate readiness risks.
• Decision Materials: Develops fact-based go/no-go recommendations, assumptions, open questions, and supporting materials for leadership review; tracks follow-up through launch gates.
Product Architecture, Filing Review & Compliance Assurance
• Forms, Rules, and Rates Review: Reviews state forms, endorsements, rating rules, and rate materials prepared by the Master MGA for consistency with documented product intent, approved risk appetite, and applicable state requirements.
• Filing Package Assurance: Checks filing packages for completeness and consistency across forms, rules, and rates; documents issues and questions for resolution before submission.
• Filing Lifecycle Tracking: Maintains a reliable inventory of submissions, objections or interrogatories, revisions, approvals, effective dates, and material status changes.
• Production Alignment: Coordinates checks that issued policy forms and rating outputs match approved filings and intended coverage; records discrepancies and routes corrective action to accountable system or MGA owners.
Connected Product Compliance
• State-by-State Usage Map: Maintains current guidance on telematics and connected-vehicle features, including permitted, restricted, or review-required uses for pricing, discounts, surcharges, coaching, renewal, cancellation, disclosures, and data usage.
• Privacy and Consumer Disclosure Research: Researches applicable insurance code, privacy, consent, retention, and consumer-disclosure requirements for connected-vehicle data.
• Feature and Launch Governance: Coordinates with Product, Data Science, Actuarial, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, and the Master MGA so feature definitions, customer notices, and operating workflows reflect approved requirements.
• Data Use Documentation: Documents proposed use of driving data in rating or underwriting workflows and facilitates required review of fairness, non-discrimination, actuarial, privacy, and jurisdiction specific considerations.
Competitive Analysis & Product Intelligence
• Product Benchmarking: Compares competitor commercial auto forms, endorsements, coverages, product introductions, and publicly available rate filings to identify coverage gaps, differentiation opportunities, and evidence needs.
• Telematics Market Intelligence: Assesses competitor use of telematics and connected-vehicle capabilities, distinguishing documented product features from claims requiring further validation.
• Actionable Recommendations: Translates findings into concise recommendations for Product, Actuarial, and leadership that address customer value, strategic fit, regulatory considerations, implementation needs, and risks.
• Benchmark Maintenance: Maintains a source-based competitor benchmark refreshed on an agreed cadence to inform product roadmap reviews.
• Regulatory watchlist, change summaries, and business-impact assessments.
• Comparable state-entry profiles, launch-readiness assessments, and prioritized rollout roadmap.
• Pre-submission filing review comments, issue log, filing inventory, and approval timeline reporting.
• Production to approved filing discrepancy tracking and resolution coordination.
• State-by-state telematics and connected-data usage map, including disclosure and feature-use requirements.
• Competitor form, coverage, rate, product, and telematics market scans with prioritized enhancement ideas.
• State research and launch readiness materials delivered to agreed planning milestones.
• Timely identification, documentation, and escalation of material regulatory and filing issues.

• Filing objections or interrogatories and approval cycle time tracked to support continuous improvement.
• Decision-ready product and competitor insights that identify leadership-prioritized opportunities.
• No regulatory fines or market-conduct findings attributable to in-scope forms or rates.
You'll have...
Bachelor’s degree in business, insurance, risk management, finance, economics, public policy, data analytics, or a related field; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
Typically 5+ years of progressive experience in insurance product development, product management, regulatory research, filing operations, compliance, market intelligence, underwriting, actuarial support, or a related commercial auto insurance discipline.
Working knowledge of commercial auto insurance products, policy forms, endorsements, rating rules, filings, state insurance regulation, and regulatory approval processes.
Experience interpreting and translating complex regulatory, product, and market information into concise, actionable business recommendations.
Strong analytical, research, written communication, and presentation skills; demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain accurate, auditable work products.
Ability to work effectively across Product, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Actuarial, Underwriting, Claims, Data Science, Technology, and external MGA partners.
